data.narrative:
Canada Rocket Company is a seed-stage space and aerospace developer founded by Hugh Kolias and David Tenny. The firm has raised $6.2M to date. The broader Space & Aerospace sector contains 5 public comparables (RKLB, PL, LUNR, ASTS, SATL) and 8 private peers including SpaceX, Rocket Lab, and ICEYE, though direct peer valuation multiples are limited at this stage and scale.

Of three valuation methods examined, only stage-progression triangulation proved applicable. Using total capital raised ($6.2M) as a value proxy and applying a 2.5x multiplier typical for seed-to-next-stage progression yields an implied valuation of $15.5M. Peer-median analysis was not executable—while 14 same-sector peers exist in the dataset, fewer than three datapoints matched narrow filters (same stage, adjacent stage, or similar valuation tier), making sector median unreliable. Public-comp anchoring could not be applied due to lack of disclosed revenue, standard for private companies.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $13M to $18M, with a median point of $16M. This range reflects modest upside from the capital raised proxy and carries material uncertainty. Primary limitations are the single applicable method and absence of comparable transaction data at the seed stage within aerospace. Revenue disclosure or a larger set of same-stage private comparables would substantially strengthen conviction.
